quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.explanation: Temporary signs in work zones always have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Increase your speed.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal three to four seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicles cannot be seen in the truck's rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses have air brakes and cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles.
Large trucks and buses always travel faster than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses have air brakes and cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses use air brakes, which work slower than the hydraulic brakes in regular cars. This means they need more time and distance to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down and look for trains. Be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not drive around the gate.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can strengthen the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can strengthen the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs increases how much they affect you. For example, one drink with a cold medicine can affect you like several drinks would alone.

questions.question: Where should you never park your vehicle?

options.text: In front of a public or private driveway.
Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
Within 30 feet of any flashing signal on the side of the roadway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You cannot park in front of a driveway, within 20 feet of a crosswalk, or within 30 feet of any stop sign, flashing signal, yield sign, or traffic control device on the roadway.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: Closer than you would behind a regular car.
Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Stay farther behind a large truck because trucks have bigger blind spots. You need extra space to be safe.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: First, use your turn signal. Then check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is entering the same lane. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop and rest or let someone else drive. Tiredness slows down your thinking and reaction time, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: What should you be aware of when approaching snow removal equipment?

options.text: You may not be able to see well.
Flying sand and ice chunks may hit your vehicle.
Keep a distance of at least 100 feet.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay 100 feet behind snow removal equipment. Sand and ice chunks can fly up and damage your car. Snow plows can reduce your visibility. Keep your distance when passing.

questions.question: When driving in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Stay alert, follow all posted signs, drive at a safe speed, and be ready to stop.
Drive faster so you don't slow down traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert, follow all posted signs, drive at a safe speed, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, stay alert and obey all posted signs. Drive at a steady speed that matches traffic flow unless signs tell you otherwise. Give workers and equipment plenty of space. Be prepared to stop at any time.

questions.question: Children up to age 18 are not allowed to ride in the cargo area of a vehicle.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Children up to age 18 cannot ride in the cargo area of a vehicle. They must be secured with a safety belt or child safety seat while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Enter slowly and let traffic already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns of a steep hill coming. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid a crash.

questions.question: You notice the driver ahead is using one hand to drive and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Keep extra distance between your car and theirs.
Understand that the other driver is not paying full attention and is more dangerous.
Not copy this driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving by talking to passengers, looking for things, reading, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to crash.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time so you get to your destination quicker.
Helps you avoid obstacles in the road.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of car crashes. It does not save time and leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: Which of these substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving ability. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups and cold medicines (which may contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines), and illegal drugs.

questions.question: If someone is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow their directions.
Do what other drivers are doing instead of listening to them.
Assume they are not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws and ignore the construction zone.

questions.explanation: When a flagger or sign directs you to slow down or change your driving in a work zone, you must obey. Ignoring these directions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and drive off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic as soon as possible.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: Which is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Tailgating another vehicle
Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment
Both of the above

questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: Before moving back to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can only safely return to your original lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, make a U-turn through the median, or swerve across lanes. These actions are illegal and dangerous.
